title: Design provenance & deprecation decision framework for tokens and surface components
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Create a reproducible, low-friction framework that captures provenance (why a token/component exists), the criteria that trigger deprecation, and an operational checklist to safely migrate consumers. Scope includes visual tokens (colors, spacing, typography), interactive primitives (buttons, inputs), and data surfaces (tables, charts).

Why: Current deprecations are ad hoc and create churn for product teams. We need clear signal paths for contributors, measurable criteria for retiring artifacts, and an automated-ish migration playbook that reduces regressions and accessibility risks. This ticket consolidates prior guidance into a single actionable framework and produces artifacts: a decision matrix doc, a contributor checklist, and a lightweight RFC template for proposed removals or major changes.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a one-page decision matrix (Confluence) that maps: provenance tags -> deprecation triggers -> recommended migration approach.
Provide a contributor-facing deprecation checklist that covers design dev, QA, docs, and release notes and includes accessibility regression tests.
Ship an RFC template for deprecation proposals with required metrics: usage telemetry, customer impact, rollout plan, fallback options.
Add a gating step in component PR templates that references the decision matrix and requires approvals from Design + Platform + Accessibility leads.
Run a pilot deprecation of a minor token (color-cta-legacy -> color-cta) using the framework and document the runbook and learnings.
Create at least two automation hooks (Slack notification for proposal creation, a spreadsheet with affected repos linked) to make review lightweight.

notes:
Trade-offs discussed: aggressive removal reduces technical debt but increases short-term consumer burden. Matrix includes tiered migration approaches: automatic aliasing (preferred for tokens with stable mapping), passthrough compatibility layer (for runtime safety), and explicit breaking changes with migration guide (only for low-usage artifacts).

Open questions: How to handle third-party integrators that pin CSS variables? Should we provide a compatibility npm package? Collect responses during RFC phase.
review_feedback: Platform: require a fallback policy in rollout (canary -> global) and an automatic revert trigger if error rate increases >1%.
Security: confirm that deprecations do not remove audit logs or alter encryption behavior; marked no security review needed for tokens but required for backend API changes.
Design Leads: prefer aliasing approach for color/tokens; reserve breaking changes for layout tokens only after cross-team sync.
